summary:
Project Cypress is a browser-based health- monitoring prototype designed for astronauts on long-duration missions. It continuously collects key indicators (heart rate, sleep, exercise, mood, isolation, radiation dose and symptoms), scores four risk domains (cardiovascular, bone & muscle, radiation, mind & mood), and runs lightweight on-device machine-learning analysis: personal trend detection, anomaly scoring against each crew member's own baseline, and a short-term

wellness forecast.
The system turns scattered readings into clear, plain-language alerts and suggested actions so astronauts can assess their own condition and act early — without waiting for a call to Earth.
Built entirely with HTML, CSS and vanilla JavaScript, the prototype runs offline after the first load, stores history locally, and requires no external servers for core analysis. It directly addresses the challenge of self-managed health monitoring in deep space while remaining transparent, interpretable and culturally grounded in Iranian design motifs.
details:
Project Cypress is a complete self-assessment and monitoring tool for astronauts. Users see live simulated vitals, complete a two-minute daily check-in (sleep, mood, resistive exercise, isolation, symptoms), and immediately receive:

An overall Wellness Index
Rule-based + model-driven alerts with plain-language actions
An ML Analysis panel showing:
Trend direction over recent check-ins (linear regression)
Anomaly score relative to the user’s personal baseline
Next-day wellness forecast
“What the model is watching” list


All analysis runs entirely in the browser. History is stored in localStorage so the model becomes more personal with each use.

Benefits & intended impact

On long missions communication delays make continuous ground support impossible. Cypress gives the crew a transparent, always-available second opinion that explains what changed, why it matters, and what to try next. It is deliberately not a medical device — it supports self-awareness and early action.
Tools & technologies

Frontend: HTML5, CSS3, vanilla JavaScript (no frameworks)

Client-side ML: simple statistical models (mean, standard deviation, linear regression slope, z-score-style anomaly detection) implemented from scratch
Visual design: custom Persian-inspired motifs (Shamse star, cypress logo, Kashi tile borders, mihrab-style frames)
Assets: Lottie animations, WebP tiles
Backend folder exists in the repository (Node.js / Express / PostgreSQL / BullMQ) but the live prototype runs fully client-side for reliability in offline scenarios

Creativity

We combined rigorous health-domain modelling with Iranian visual culture so the tool feels both scientifically serious and personally meaningful. The on-device ML approach means the system works even when communication with Earth is delayed or unavailable.
